<a id="consoleeventmap"></a>

## `ConsoleEventMap`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleEventMap` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The single decision point for "does this bus event belong on the console, and what does it look like there". One owner per event kind.

Two ways an event gets a console line, in this order:

1. The producer named its own [`ConsolePayload.TagKey`](#consolepayload--tagkey), [`ConsolePayload.PrimaryKey`](#consolepayload--primarykey) and field order. Every feature that can edit its own emit site does this.
2. The canonical table below, for the events whose payload is a Core event record's own `Fields()` and therefore cannot carry console members (`event/*`, `satone/speech`, `satone/state`) and for the health/Unity streams.

Anything else - ticks, `phase=` diagnostics, polling notices, aggregates - is file-only, and a producer can always force that with `("mirror", false)`.

The code-mod tags ([`ConsoleTags.Mods`](#consoletags--mods), [`ConsoleTags.Mod`](#consoletags--mod)) and the Phases D-S tags ([`ConsoleTags.Action`](#consoletags--action), [`ConsoleTags.Api`](#consoletags--api), [`ConsoleTags.Script`](#consoletags--script), [`ConsoleTags.Trigger`](#consoletags--trigger), [`ConsoleTags.Cond`](#consoletags--cond), [`ConsoleTags.Audio`](#consoletags--audio), [`ConsoleTags.UiSkin`](#consoletags--uiskin), [`ConsoleTags.EditData`](#consoletags--editdata), [`ConsoleTags.Mic`](#consoletags--mic), [`ConsoleTags.Camera`](#consoletags--camera)) take the first way only: their producers name the tag, so the canonical table below has no rows for them. A `ConditionsChanged` event on the game bus stays file-only (the `default` branch).

<a id="consoleeventmap--unfocusedfield"></a>

### `const string UnfocusedField = "unfocused"`

Payload member a producer sets when a bad reading is the window's fault.

<a id="consoleeventmap--canonical"></a>

### `static ConsoleRecord Canonical(DateTimeOffset time, string sys, string name, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object> payload)`

The canonical record for an event whose producer cannot name its own layout, or null when the event is file-only.

- `name`: Bus event name.
- `payload`: Event payload.

<a id="consoleeventmap--trymap"></a>

### `static bool TryMap(BusEvent evt, out ConsoleRecord record)`

Builds the console record for one bus event, or returns false for a file-only event.

**Parameters**

- `evt`: The published event.
- `record`: The record to print, or null.

<a id="consoleeventmap--withouttagecho"></a>

### `static string WithoutTagEcho(string tag, string primary)`

Drops a leading "`TAG:`" from a primary that repeats its own tag, so a summary written for a plain log (`PACKS: 2 loaded ...`) does not print as `PACKS PACKS: 2 loaded ...`. Only the exact tag followed by a colon is dropped, with the spaces after it; anything else, or a primary that would be left empty, is returned unchanged.

**Parameters**

- `tag`: The record's tag, e.g. `PACKS`.
- `primary`: The primary text.

**Returns:** The primary without the echo, or `primary` unchanged.

## `ConsoleEvents`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleEvents` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How a producer publishes an event that has a console line: once, on [`TraceBus`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Bus.md#tracebus), naming its own tag, primary column and field order.

Before these helpers, every feature did the same thing twice - `Log.LogInfo(pretty text)` for the console and `TraceBus.EmitFields(the same event)` for the file - which is why one spoken sentence cost 23 console lines. These helpers are the one way to publish now: the trace file gets the full payload, and the console gets exactly the columns named here.

<a id="consolelogfilter"></a>

## `ConsoleLogFilter`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleLogFilter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Which BepInEx log lines the framework's two console sinks keep: `cwy-console.log` (`CwyConsoleListener`) and the in-game console's scrollback (`ConsoleLogListener`). One rule for both, so the file and the overlay can never disagree about what was logged.

The rule: an Error or Fatal from any source is kept - a Unity exception from the game matters even though its source is not ours. Otherwise the source must be one of ours (its name starts with [`ConsoleLogFilter.CwySourcePrefix`](#consolelogfilter--cwysourceprefix)) and the level must not be Debug; the trace file is where that level of detail belongs. Core cannot reference BepInEx, so the caller translates its `LogLevel` into the two flags.

<a id="consolelogfilter--cwysourceprefix"></a>

### `const string CwySourcePrefix = "CWY"`

Source-name prefix that marks a log source as the framework's own.

<a id="consolelogfilter--admits"></a>

True when a console sink should keep the line.

**Parameters**

- `sourceName`: BepInEx source name, e.g. `CWYLS Game Adapter`; null when unknown.
- `isErrorOrFatal`: The line was logged at Error or Fatal.
- `isDebug`: The line was logged at Debug (or at the catch-all level).

<a id="consolerecordformatter"></a>

## `ConsoleRecordFormatter`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleRecordFormatter` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Renders a [`ConsoleRecord`](#consolerecord) as the one canonical console line, and renders single values the same way everywhere.

Grammar:

```csharp
<line>    ::= HH:mm:ss.fff  SP SP  TAG  SP SP  <primary>  [ SP SP <fields> ]
<primary> ::= free text, never two consecutive spaces, never a newline
<fields>  ::= k=v ( SP k=v )*   v = bare token | "quoted" | -
```

Rules that make it parseable and stable:

1. Two spaces separate the three columns; single spaces are free inside the primary and inside a quoted value.
2. A value that is empty, or contains a space, a quote, a backslash or an `=`, is double-quoted with `\"` escaping. A null value is `-`.
3. One physical line per event: newlines become [`ConsoleRecord.NewlineGlyph`](#consolerecord--newlineglyph).
4. The stamp is the event time, not the time the line reached the sink.

<a id="consolerecordformatter--columnseparator"></a>

### `const string ColumnSeparator = "  "`

The column separator: two spaces.

<a id="consolerecordformatter--timeformat"></a>

### `const string TimeFormat = "HH:mm:ss.fff"`

The time format every line starts with.

<a id="consolerecordformatter--format"></a>

### `static string Format(ConsoleRecord record)`

Renders the record as one physical line, without a trailing newline.

**Parameters**

- `record`: The record. Null returns an empty string rather than throwing.

<a id="consolerecordformatter--primary"></a>

### `static string Primary(string primary)`

The primary column: one line, never two consecutive spaces (they would be read as a column break), capped at [`ConsoleRecord.PrimaryLimit`](#consolerecord--primarylimit).

**Parameters**

- `primary`: The raw primary text; null or blank becomes `-`.

<a id="consolerecordformatter--value"></a>

### `static string Value(string value)`

One field value: `-` when missing, quoted when it could not be read back as a bare token, otherwise as it stands.

**Parameters**

- `value`: The raw value; null or empty becomes `-`.

## `ConsoleRecordParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleRecordParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Reads a console line back into a [`ConsoleRecord`](#consolerecord) - the same grammar [`ConsoleRecordFormatter`](#consolerecordformatter) writes, so the sink, the in-game console and `tools/mac/watch-log.py` can never drift apart.

The C# parser and the Python one in the viewer are kept honest by a shared golden corpus: the unit tests write `tools/mac/tests/console-golden.txt` and the viewer is run over it with `--strict`.

<a id="consolerecordparser--levelof"></a>

**Parameters**

- `tag`: A console tag.

<a id="consolerecordparser--parsefields"></a>

Splits a `k=v k="v v"` run into ordered fields. Never throws.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The field column of a line.

<a id="consolerecordparser--tryparse-string-ref-consolerecord"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(string line, out ConsoleRecord record)`

Reads one line. Returns false for anything that is not a console record.

**Parameters**

- `line`: The physical line, with or without a trailing newline.
- `record`: The parsed record, or null.

<a id="consolerecordparser--tryparse-string-datetimeoffset-ref-consolerecord"></a>

### `static bool TryParse(string line, DateTimeOffset reference, out ConsoleRecord record)`

Reads one line, dating it from `reference`. The grammar carries a time of day and no date, so the caller decides which day the line belongs to (the sink and the viewer both read a live file, so "today" is right for them).

**Parameters**

- `line`: The physical line.
- `reference`: Supplies the date and the UTC offset of the parsed time.
- `record`: The parsed record, or null.

<a id="consoletags"></a>

## `ConsoleTags`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Logging.ConsoleTags` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The one-word console tags. One tag per event family; the viewer maps tag to colour, so a two-word tag would make the grammar ambiguous.

Everything a person watching the game should see has a tag here. Anything not in this list - ticks, `phase=` diagnostics, polling notices, per-keystroke input, aggregates - stays in the trace file. The rule: the console answers "what happened in the game", the trace file answers "what did our code do about it".

A tag is `[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,11}` (the viewer's grammar). Every tag here has a colour in `tools/mac/watch-log.py` (`TAGS`); `LoggingConsoleTagsTests` keeps the two lists equal. The feature tags further down are named by their producers (`ConsoleEvents.Emit` with the tag), so [`ConsoleEventMap`](#consoleeventmap) needs no rows for them.

<a id="consoletags--uiskin"></a>

### `const string UiSkin = "UISKIN"`

Pack sprites were applied to the game's UI, or restored (D-UI).

<a id="consoletags--unity"></a>

### `const string Unity = "UNITY"`

A Unity error, exception or failed assertion.

<a id="consoletags--unknown"></a>

### `const string Unknown = "NOTE"`

What a record with no usable tag prints as.

<a id="consoletags--voice"></a>

### `const string Voice = "VOICE"`

A voice clip was registered or played.

<a id="consoletags--warn"></a>

### `const string Warn = "WARN"`

A direct `LogWarning` the sink wrapped.

<a id="consoletags--window"></a>

### `const string Window = "WINDOW"`

A window view was switched on or off.

<a id="consoletags--all"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> All { get; }`

Every tag above, in declaration order. For parity checks (viewer colours, the in-game console's families) and documentation.
